rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4 and Figs 9-10 - the authors develop a soil-water-balance/stochastic model generating daily volumes and hourly demand hydrographs at hydrant and upstream level, and compare simulated with Venturimeter-measured volumes (1990-1999) and hourly discharges (10-day peak period of 1999) for district 10 of the Sinistra Ofanto scheme, Southern Italy.
rows.notes: The study reports no result on the investment cost of on-demand networks nor on the guarantee of water supply during peak periods. What it shows is that a water-balance plus stochastic farmer-behaviour model can reproduce measured daily withdrawn volumes well and hourly peak-period hydrographs with similar patterns, though with occasional simulated hourly peaks higher than measured because hydraulic constraints of the network are not modelled. Its only link to the claim is that the generated peak-period demand hydrographs are intended as inputs for designing or analysing on-demand networks (a precondition for sizing a network that guarantees peak supply); cost is never mentioned. The claim is therefore not supported by this study's own findings.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a model-development and calibration paper on an on-demand pressurised scheme in Italy; it contains no economic or cost analysis.
